title: Sail trim on a cruising yacht: telltales, twist and balance
lead: Good trim makes a cruising yacht faster, flatter and lighter on the helm, and it uses only a handful of lines. Here is what each control does, how to read the telltales, and how to stop the boat under sail by heaving-to.
description: Sail trim on a cruising yacht: mainsheet, traveller, genoa cars, halyards, outhaul and kicker, reading telltales, twist, trim from close-hauled to a run, weather helm, heaving-to and short-handed tips.
summary: The sheets set the angle of each sail, and the cars, kicker, outhaul and halyards set its shape.
Trim the genoa until the telltales on both sides stream back, and move the car until they break evenly.
A little weather helm is right; heavy weather helm means ease the traveller, flatten the main or reef.
To heave-to, tack without releasing the genoa sheet, then lock the wheel as if to head up.
